title: Translating a ball into a larger ball does not increase a lintegral
statement: Let n be a natural number, F : R^n -> [0,infinity] an arbitrary function (no measurability assumed), r, s real numbers and w in R^n with r + |w| <= s. Then int^-_(B_r) F(x - w) dx <= int^-_(B_s) F(x) dx, where B_rho := ball(0,rho) is the open ball of EuclideanSpace R (Fin n) (empty if rho <= 0), dx is Lebesgue measure (volume) and int^- is Mathlib's lintegral.
lean_statement: ∀ (n : ℕ) (F : Rn n → ℝ≥0∞) (r s : ℝ) (w : Rn n), r + ‖w‖ ≤ s → ∫⁻ x in ball (0 : Rn n) r, F (x - w) ≤ ∫⁻ x in ball (0 : Rn n) s, F x
